sources: China regarded UNISFA as important for stability and political progress in Abyei. It supported renewing the mandate and voted in favour of resolution 2760 (2024). China called for broader consultation in the new strategic assessment and criticized putting the draft to a vote despite remaining differences.

Russia abstained on resolution 2760 (2024) while describing UNISFA's work as important and necessary. It objected to provisions it regarded as unrelated or politicized and urged dialogue between mission leadership and the governments in Port Sudan and Juba.
proposals: China and Russia both regarded UNISFA's work as important in Abyei.

sources: China welcomed the one-year renewal of MINUSCA in resolution 2800 (2025) and voted in favour. It said the extension would facilitate elections at all levels, backed the mission's continued work and urged it to concentrate limited resources on the most pressing tasks.

The United States abstained on resolution 2800 (2025), saying the one-year extension and troop ceiling did not adequately reflect priorities. It proposed extending MINUSCA for six months to assess the implications of elections, and was willing to negotiate a twelve-month renewal if conditions were met.
